q: Green copper(II) carbonate is heated in a test tube. It turns black as copper(II) oxide forms and carbon dioxide is given off. What type of reaction is this?
options: exothermic, because the solid changes colour
exothermic, because energy is continuously taken in from the burner
endothermic, because energy is continuously taken in from the burner
endothermic, because energy is released to the burner
explain: Thermal decomposition needs a continual supply of heat, so it is endothermic.

q: On a labelled reaction pathway diagram for an endothermic reaction, which two features are always drawn?
options: an arrow for Ea from the reactants level up to the peak, and an arrow for ΔH upward from the reactants level to the higher products level
an arrow for Ea from the reactants level to the products level, and an arrow for ΔH from the reactants level up to the peak
an arrow for Ea from the products level to the peak, and an arrow for ΔH downward from the reactants level to the lower products level
an arrow for Ea from the reactants level up to the peak, and an arrow for ΔH downward from the reactants level to the lower products level
explain: For endothermic reactions the products sit above the reactants, so ΔH points up; Ea is always measured from the reactants to the peak.

q: A reaction pathway diagram shows reactants at 20 kJ/mol and products at 90 kJ/mol. What does the diagram show?
options: an endothermic reaction that takes in 70 kJ/mol from the surroundings
an endothermic reaction that takes in 110 kJ/mol from the surroundings
an exothermic reaction that releases 70 kJ/mol to the surroundings
an exothermic reaction that releases 110 kJ/mol to the surroundings
explain: The products are higher than the reactants by 90 − 20 = 70 kJ/mol, so 70 kJ/mol is absorbed.

q: What is the energy change for the process Cl₂(g) → 2Cl(g), given that the Cl–Cl bond energy is 243 kJ/mol?
options: +243 kJ/mol
+486 kJ/mol
−486 kJ/mol
−243 kJ/mol
explain: Breaking one mole of Cl–Cl bonds is endothermic and requires 243 kJ.

q: Which process is endothermic?
options: respiration in living cells
the neutralisation of hydrochloric acid by sodium hydroxide
the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate
the burning of magnesium in air
explain: Calcium carbonate only decomposes if thermal energy is continually supplied, so it is endothermic.

q: On a labelled reaction pathway diagram for an exothermic reaction, in which direction does the arrow for ΔH point?
options: upwards, from the level of the reactants to the top of the curve
upwards, from the level of the reactants to the level of the products
downwards, from the top of the curve to the horizontal axis
downwards, from the level of the reactants to the level of the products
explain: ΔH is the change in energy from reactants to products; for an exothermic reaction the products are lower, so the arrow points down.

q: Fireworks burn quickly and give out heat, light and sound. Which statement about the chemical reactions is correct?
options: They are endothermic because the temperature rises.
They are exothermic because energy is taken in from the surroundings.
They are endothermic because light energy is produced.
They are exothermic because energy is transferred to the surroundings.
explain: Heat, light and sound are all forms of energy released to the surroundings.

q: Why does a candle flame keep the surrounding air warm?
options: The wax is a reactant that stores thermal energy only.
The combustion of wax is exothermic and absorbs thermal energy.
The combustion of wax is exothermic and releases thermal energy.
The combustion of wax is endothermic and releases thermal energy.
explain: Combustion transfers thermal energy to the surroundings.

q: Which row correctly describes an exothermic reaction in terms of bond energies?
options: negative | energy to break bonds is greater than energy released making bonds
positive | energy to break bonds is equal to energy released making bonds
positive | energy to break bonds is less than energy released making bonds
negative | energy to break bonds is less than energy released making bonds
explain: In an exothermic reaction ΔH = broken − made is negative because making bonds releases more energy.

q: Which row correctly describes an endothermic reaction?
columns: Energy of products compared with reactants
options: thermal energy given out to surroundings | temperature of surroundings increases | energy of products higher than reactants
thermal energy taken in from surroundings | temperature of surroundings increases | energy of products lower than reactants
thermal energy taken in from surroundings | temperature of surroundings decreases | energy of products higher than reactants
thermal energy given out to surroundings | temperature of surroundings decreases | energy of products higher than reactants
explain: In an endothermic reaction energy goes in, the surroundings cool and the products end up higher in energy.

q: Which of these changes would show a temperature decrease if carried out in an insulated cup?
options: magnesium reacting with dilute sulfuric acid
sodium hydroxide dissolving in water
ammonium chloride dissolving in water
calcium oxide reacting with water
explain: Dissolving ammonium chloride is endothermic; the other three give out heat.

q: Which statement about a reaction pathway diagram of an exothermic reaction is correct?
options: The temperature of the surroundings falls because the products are at a higher energy level than the reactants.
The temperature of the surroundings rises because the products are at a higher energy level than the reactants.
The temperature of the surroundings rises because the products are at a lower energy level than the reactants.
The temperature of the surroundings falls because the products are at a lower energy level than the reactants.
explain: The energy lost by the chemicals is gained by the surroundings, which warm up.

q: How many moles of O–H bonds are formed when 1 mol of methane burns completely in oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water, CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O?
options: 1 mol
8 mol
4 mol
2 mol
explain: Each H₂O has two O–H bonds and 2 mol of water are formed, so 2 × 2 = 4 mol of O–H bonds.

q: Which observation would a student expect when ammonium nitrate dissolves in water in a beaker?
options: The beaker feels warm because thermal energy is given out to the surroundings.
The beaker feels cold because thermal energy is taken in from the surroundings.
The beaker feels warm because thermal energy is taken in from the surroundings.
The beaker feels cold because thermal energy is given out to the surroundings.
explain: Dissolving ammonium nitrate is endothermic, so the water and the beaker cool.

q: Which of these correctly pairs a process with the effect on the temperature of its surroundings?
options: thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate: increases
burning ethanol: increases
photosynthesis: increases
burning ethanol: decreases
explain: Burning ethanol is exothermic so the surroundings warm; the other two absorb energy.

q: Solid sodium hydroxide dissolves in water and the beaker becomes warm. What type of change is this?
options: exothermic, because thermal energy is absorbed from the surroundings
exothermic, because thermal energy is released to the surroundings
endothermic, because the solid disappears
endothermic, because thermal energy is released to the surroundings
explain: A warming beaker shows thermal energy is released, so dissolving sodium hydroxide is exothermic.

q: Which statement explains why a reaction is endothermic in terms of bonds?
options: More energy is needed to break the bonds in the reactants than is released when bonds form in the products.
Bond making takes in energy and bond breaking releases energy.
Energy is released when the bonds in the reactants break.
More energy is released when bonds form in the products than is needed to break the bonds in the reactants.
explain: A net absorption of energy occurs when bond breaking costs more than bond making returns.

q: Use the bond energies (N≡N 945, O=O 498, N=O 630, all in kJ/mol) to calculate ΔH for N₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2NO(g).
options: +183 kJ/mol
+1443 kJ/mol
−183 kJ/mol
−1260 kJ/mol

q: Which equation represents an exothermic reaction?
options: C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g)
CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g)
CuCO₃(s) → CuO(s) + CO₂(g)
6CO₂(g) + 6H₂O(l) → C₆H₁₂O₆(aq) + 6O₂(g)
explain: Burning carbon in oxygen is combustion, which is exothermic; the others take in energy.

q: Which statement about breaking and making bonds when hydrogen burns, 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, is correct?
options: H–H and O=O bonds are broken, releasing energy, and O–H bonds are formed, taking in energy.
H–H and O=O bonds are broken, taking in energy, and O–H bonds are formed, releasing energy.
H–H and O=O bonds are formed, releasing energy, and O–H bonds are broken, taking in energy.
Only O–H bonds are involved and no bonds are broken.
explain: In the reactants the H–H and O=O bonds are broken (endothermic); in the product the new O–H bonds form (exothermic).

q: The enthalpy change for burning 1 mol of hydrogen in oxygen is written as ΔH = −286 kJ/mol. What does the negative sign tell you?
options: The reaction needs a catalyst.
Thermal energy is released to the surroundings.
Thermal energy is taken in from the surroundings.
The activation energy is negative.
explain: A negative ΔH is the sign of an exothermic reaction.

q: Calcium carbonate must be heated strongly the whole time for it to decompose; if heating stops, the decomposition stops. Why?
options: The reaction is exothermic, so the energy released stops the reaction.
The reaction is endothermic, so it continuously gives out thermal energy to the surroundings.
The reaction is exothermic, so it continuously needs thermal energy from the surroundings.
The reaction is endothermic, so it continuously needs thermal energy from the surroundings.
explain: Endothermic reactions take in energy, so they carry on only while energy is supplied.

q: Use the bond energies (C=C 614, Br–Br 193, C–C 347, C–Br 285, all in kJ/mol) to calculate ΔH for C₂H₄(g) + Br₂(g) → C₂H₄Br₂(g).
options: −110 kJ/mol
−917 kJ/mol
−807 kJ/mol
+110 kJ/mol

q: Which row correctly links an observation to the type of reaction?
options: temperature of mixture falls | endothermic | energy taken in from surroundings
temperature of mixture falls | exothermic | energy given out to surroundings
temperature of mixture rises | endothermic | energy given out to surroundings
temperature of mixture rises | endothermic | energy taken in from surroundings
explain: A falling temperature indicates an endothermic reaction that absorbs energy from its surroundings.

q: Reaction X and reaction Y both have ΔH = −100 kJ/mol. Reaction X has Ea = 60 kJ/mol and reaction Y has Ea = 120 kJ/mol. Which statement is correct?
options: Both reactions are endothermic.
They release the same energy overall, but at a given temperature X has more particles able to react.
Y releases more energy overall because its activation energy is greater.
X releases more energy overall because its activation energy is less.
explain: ΔH is the same so the overall energy released is the same; the lower Ea of X means a larger fraction of collisions are successful.

q: Which is a use of an exothermic reaction?
options: growing crops by photosynthesis
using ammonium nitrate in an instant cold pack
burning natural gas to heat a home
decomposing limestone to make quicklime
explain: Burning natural gas gives out thermal energy; the other uses involve reactions that take in energy.

q: Use the bond energies (C–H 413, Cl–Cl 243, C–Cl 339, H–Cl 432, all in kJ/mol) to calculate ΔH for CH₄(g) + Cl₂(g) → CH₃Cl(g) + HCl(g).
options: +115 kJ/mol
−115 kJ/mol
+656 kJ/mol
−771 kJ/mol

q: On a reaction pathway diagram for any reaction, where are the reactants shown?
options: on the vertical axis, at the bottom
at the right-hand end of the curve, after the reaction is finished
at the left-hand end of the curve, on the horizontal line before the reaction starts
at the top of the curve, at the highest point
explain: The pathway reads from left to right: reactants first, then the climb to the peak, then the products.

q: The equation for photosynthesis is 6CO₂(g) + 6H₂O(l) → C₆H₁₂O₆(aq) + 6O₂(g). Which statement is correct?
options: The reaction is exothermic because oxygen is produced.
The reaction is endothermic because it takes in energy from sunlight.
The reaction is endothermic because it gives out energy to the plant.
The reaction is exothermic because it takes in energy from sunlight.
explain: Photosynthesis absorbs energy from light, so it is endothermic.

q: A hand warmer contains iron powder that reacts with oxygen from the air and gets warm. What does this show about the reaction?
options: It is exothermic because thermal energy is released to the surroundings.
It is endothermic because oxygen is used up.
It is exothermic because thermal energy is taken in from the air.
It is endothermic because the pack becomes warm.
explain: The pack warms up because the reaction gives out thermal energy, which is exothermic.
